newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU WEAKER, SEEN DIPPING FURTHER.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU WEAKER, SEEN DIPPING FURTHER.

text.p: Romania's leu ended Tuesday lower at 6,800/850 to the dollar after idling at 6,700/750 throughout the day on a market facing dollar squeezes, and traders awaited further lows amid rising inflationary fears.
"The leu will soon breach the 7,000 level but that price will not have a psychological impact on the market given the expectations for quicker inflation," said a trader with a dealer bank.
Romania's government announced on Tuesday that year-on-year inflation was expected to quicken to 97 percent this year from 56.9 percent in 1996.
It said inflation would blip to some 41 percent in the first quarter of 1997, led by January's fuel price hike and expected electricity and food price rises but it would calm down toward year's end.
Traders said the leu's retail rates had already touched the 7,000 level with licensed money changing bureaux' prices easing to 6,650/7,000 against 6,400/6,750 in the morning.
Operators said intrabank trading saw higher volumes but interbank turnover stayed scarce. Latest data put interbank volume at $353,200 on Monday when overall trading was $12.6 million.
Trading on the money market remained thin with most players chasing leu funds and overnight funds at about 87-88 percent.
